“I’ll thank to keep your hands off my things,” the Spy said, reading Sniper’s mind. “I have more use for them than you.”“我劝你别碰我的东西，”间谍读出了狙击手的心思，“我比你更用得上它们。”

“Sure. Developed by BLU?”“当然。BLU 研发的？”

“Of course. A gentler formula is about to be released to the public.”“当然。一种更温和的配方即将向公众发布。”

“I should hope it’s gentler. Those things are a menace.” And BLU would probably make more money with those little miracles than they ever would with gravel and lumber. Sniper yawned. “So you been a good little guinea pig for ‘em or did you just nick them for yerself?”“但愿它确实更温和些。那玩意儿可是个祸害。”而且 BLU 靠那些小奇迹赚的钱，恐怕会比靠碎石和木材赚的还多。狙击手打了个哈欠。“所以你是给他们乖乖当小白鼠了，还是只是给自己顺走了几个？”

The Spy smiled.间谍笑了。

Bo snorted awake. “Wassat ‘bout bein’ able to buy boner pills? Ow.”博哼了一声醒了过来。“刚说能买壮阳药是咋回事？哎哟。”

“Shh. Don’t move too much, mon beau. You must be exhausted.”“ Shh。别乱动，mon beau。你一定累坏了。”

“Yeah, I’m, um…” Bo paused, shifting on Spy’s torso. “Oh, hell, Frenchie, you’re still up. I don’t think I can–”“是啊，我，呃……” Bo 顿了顿，在 Spy 的躯干上挪了挪身子。“噢，见鬼，法国佬，你还硬着呢。我觉得我受不了——”

“Don’t worry,” the Spy assured him as he stroked his face. “It’s this other one’s fault I was given a bigger dose than either of you. This is a mere physiological effect. Those pills grant ability, not desire. But I wouldn’t reject a petit bisou from you.”“别担心，” Spy 抚摸着他的脸，安慰道。“都怪另一个家伙，给我用的剂量比你们俩谁都大。这不过是生理反应罢了。那些药丸赋予的是能力，不是欲望。不过，我不会拒绝你给我的 petit bisou。”

Bo didn’t need to understand French to know what that meant. He happily slid up to the Spy and the petit bisou turned into a nice show. When Bo tried to do something about the Spy’s ongoing state, his hand was gently brushed aside.博不需要懂法语，也能明白那是什么意思。他高高兴兴地蹭到间谍身边，petit bisou于是变成了一场好戏。当博想对间谍那一直没消下去的状态做点什么时，他的手被轻轻拨开了。

“Don’t push yourself, mon beau,” the Spy said, running his thumb over Bo’s knuckles. “Truly, I feel wonderfully sated. Even I need rest after a good lovemaking session, priapism aside.”“别勉强自己，mon beau，”间谍说，拇指摩挲着 Bo 的指关节，“说真的，我感觉无比满足。就算是我，在一场痛快的云雨之后也需要休息——勃起异常什么的就先不提了。”

Bloody hell, he ought to, but one couldn’t be sure with the BLU Spy. Sniper wasn’t sure that the spook would have extended the same courtesy to him, no matter how chafed and exhausted he was. If he tried anything, the Spy was going to have to carry his own bits back to the BLU base in a bucket of motel ice. The Spy snapped his fingers.该死的，他确实该休息，可面对 BLU 间谍，谁也说不准。狙击手也不确定这鬼鬼祟祟的家伙会不会也对他讲这份体贴，不管他自己被磨得多么生疼、累成什么样。他要是敢乱来，这间谍就得把自己的那话儿装进汽车旅馆的冰桶里，自己拎回 BLU 基地。间谍打了个响指。

“Chien. Cigarettes, if you please.”“ Chien。请把香烟递给我。”

“Get ‘em yerself,” Sniper answered, bristling.“你自己去拿，”狙击手恼火地答道。

“Jeez, he can’t move after what we did to him, Shan,” Bo said. “Sorry. I can do it.”“天啊，我们把他弄成那样，他现在动不了，Shan，” Bo 说。“抱歉，我来吧。”

“Non, non, let the other fetch. It’s all his fault.” The Spy didn’t bother to look at Sniper, more concerned with kissing Bo along the jaw. “Mannboro’s will do.”“ Non, non，让另一个去拿吧。都是他的错。”间谍懒得看狙击手一眼，只顾着顺着 Bo 的下颌亲吻。“曼宝路就行。”

Squeezing himself out from under their combined weight, Sniper fetched. He watched them pash for a bit before giving Spy a cig and taking his turn with Bo. Then more smoking and more kissing and petting while whoever was the third party watched and smoked contentedly. It was a cozy little set-up. Eventually, of course, it had to end. Bo was the first to make a move, standing on shaky legs to get dressed.狙击手从他们两人合压的重量下挤出身子，去拿了点东西。他看着他们亲热了一会儿，然后递给间谍一支烟，轮到他跟波亲热。接着又是更多的抽烟、接吻和抚摸，而剩下的那个人则心满意足地边看边抽。这局面挺温馨惬意。当然，最终总得结束。波最先有了动作，颤颤巍巍地站起来穿衣服。

“Guess I should hit the road. Well, not the road-the road yet, but yeah… Head on home.”看来我该上路了。嗯，倒不是真的上那条路——还没到上路的时候，不过……回家去喽。

“Mm,” said Sniper.“嗯，”狙击手说。

“I hope we’ll have a chance to meet again before you depart. If not,” Spy said, sitting up with some difficulty and taking hold of Bo’s hand. “Forgive me for being unable to stand. I’ll carry the memory of this night with you with me always, mon beau. Bon voyage.”“我希望在你启程之前，我们还能有机会再见一面。如果不行的话，”斯派说着，有些吃力地坐起身，握住博的手，“请原谅我站不起来。我会永远把与你共度的这个夜晚的回忆带在身边，mon beau。Bon voyage。”

“Oh my God, Frenchie, that’s so goddamn corny,” Bo said, laughing. Still, he blushed and smiled broadly when the Spy kissed his hand with a wink. He drew his hand back at looked over to Sniper. “Hope to see ya too before I leave, then, Shan.”“我的天哪，Frenchie，这也太他妈肉麻了，” Bo 笑着说。可当 Spy 朝他眨了眨眼、吻了吻他的手时，他还是脸红了，笑得格外灿烂。他抽回手，看向 Sniper。“那希望我走之前也能见到你，Shan。”

“Yeah.”“是啊。”

Bo looked at him expectantly. Sniper felt the Spy tense next to him as he smoked.波满怀期待地看着他。狙击手抽着烟，感觉到身旁的间谍绷紧了身体。

“Cheers,” he added.“干杯，”他补充道。

“Yeah…” Bo said. He went to the door. “Bye.”“嗯……”波说。他走向门口。“再见。”

The door shut. All of a sudden the room felt very, very cold. Sniper was looked over to the Spy, who was glaring spycicles at him.门关上了。突然间，房间变得非常、非常冷。狙击手朝间谍看去，而间谍正朝他射来间谍冰锥般的眼刀。

“That was the worst thing I’ve ever seen,” he said. He inhaled deeply from his cigarette. “Absolutely deplorable. A travesty.”“那是我见过的最糟糕的事，”他说。他深深吸了一口烟。“简直糟透了。一场闹剧。”

“What?”“什么？”

“Cheers, he says. Really?”“干杯，”他说。“真的吗？”

“Yeah.”“是啊。”

“Idiot.”“白痴。”

“Mm.”“嗯。”

“Don’t mm at me, you heartless savage. For somebody whose job is to watch, you’re terrible at noticing.” The Spy glanced at the closed motel door. “He’s deeply smitten with you. Parbleu, have some feeling.”“别拿嗯声敷衍我，你这个没心没肺的野蛮人。一个吃盯梢这碗饭的人，居然这么不会察言观色。”间谍瞥了一眼紧闭的汽车旅馆房门。“他可是对你痴迷得很。Parbleu,你倒是有点感情啊。”

“It’s just a bit of fun.”“只是图个乐子罢了。”

“Hound.”“猎狗。”

“Like you’re any better. I’ll carry the memory of you with me always shit. Rubbish. How many lays have you fed that line to? He laughed at it, you know.”“说得好像你多好似的。我会把你的记忆带在身边直到永远——这种屁话。垃圾。这句台词你拿去哄过多少个床伴了？他听了都笑了，你知道吧。”

The BLU Spy raised an eyebrow at him, haughty but not offended. “You’re such an amateur. Don’t you know that half of seizing someone’s heart isn’t in the sex, but the laughter?”BLU 间谍朝他挑了挑眉，神情高傲却并未动怒。“你可真是个外行。难道你不知道，俘获一个人的心，有一半靠的不是性，而是笑声吗？”

Sniper laughed. Bitterly. “Right. I’m sure he sees a happily-ever-after with ya.”狙击手笑了。笑得很苦涩。“是啊。我敢肯定他觉得自己能跟你有个幸福美满的结局。”

“Mysterious men in masks are flings, not long-term lovers,” the Spy said, with groan-worthy self-importance. He continued to smoke Sniper’s cigarettes. “And you heard how he described me: classy, rich, glamorous… Leagues above his level, in every way. That man may not be very bright, but he still understands that about me, deep down. I’m a memory of excitement in his humdrum hayseed life. I’m not real. But you…” He gave Sniper a dismissive once-over. “Common, sun-baked, working-class schmo with dirt under his nails and a hideous, dust-stained vehicle. So down-to-earth. So ordinary. Just like him.”“戴面具的神秘男人只适合当露水情缘，不是长久伴侣，”间谍带着令人扶额的自命不凡说道。他继续抽着狙击手的烟。“而且你也听见他是怎么形容我的了：有格调、有钱、光彩照人……方方面面都甩他好几条街。那家伙也许不太聪明，但内心深处，他还是明白我这一点的。我不过是他那单调乏味的乡巴佬生活里一段刺激的回忆。我并不真实。可你……”他不屑地把狙击手从头到脚打量了一遍。“一个普普通通、被太阳晒得黝黑、指甲缝里全是泥的工人阶级蠢货，还开着辆丑得要命、满是灰尘的车。多么接地气。多么普通。简直跟他一模一样。”

Sniper bristled. “I’m nothin’ like a civilian who couldn’t shoot his way out of a wet paper bag.”狙击手顿时炸毛了。“我跟那种枪法烂到连湿纸袋都打不穿的平民可一点都不像。”

“Yes, I know that, you know that, but does he? But what could I have expected from you? A heartbreaker and he isn’t even trying. He would impress me if he did it with any flair at all. How disappointing of him. Always I’m disappointed by him.”“是啊，我知道，你知道，可他知道吗？可我还能指望你什么呢？一个负心汉，而且他根本都没刻意去当。他要是稍微有点派头，我倒是会佩服他。他真令人失望。他总是让我失望。”

“Why do you even care?”“你到底为什么要在意？”

The sound of Bo’s ute starting up, then stalling. Then stalling again.博的皮卡传来发动的声音，接着熄火了。然后又熄火了。

“Deus ex machina,” the Spy said. “Or deus ex hideous vehicle. Be a gentleman and go help him, or I’ll put out my cigarette in your eye. Give the farewell he deserves. Something with more than one syllable. Pretend to put some romance into it. Good God, but you are truly an amateur at this.”“机械降神，”间谍说，“或者是从那辆丑得吓人的车里出来的神。做回绅士，去帮帮他，不然我就把烟头摁灭在你眼睛里。给他一个配得上他的告别。说点不止一个音节的词。假装一下，往里头添点浪漫。老天爷，你干这个真是十足的外行。”

“Fine,” Sniper said, looking for his clothes. “Only to get away from your nagging, you woman.”“好吧，”狙击手一边找自己的衣服一边说，“就为了躲开你这女人的唠叨。”

Outside, Bo had popped the hood of his truck and was checking the motor. He looked up at Sniper when he heard him approach and shrugged bashfully.外面，博已经掀开他卡车的引擎盖，正在检查发动机。听到斯奈珀走近，他抬起头，腼腆地耸了耸肩。

“Told ya it was a piece of junk.”“早跟你说了吧，那就是个破玩意儿。”

“Hm. What’s the problem?”“嗯。有什么问题吗？”

“Battery died. Again. Give me a jump?”“电瓶又没电了。再帮我搭个电？”

“Yeah.”“是啊。”

An easy fix. They got the truck sputtering back to life, coughing black smoke out of its tailpipe. It really was on its last legs.修起来不难。他们让卡车突突地重新发动起来，排气管里咳出一股股黑烟。这辆卡车确实已经快不行了。

“Thanks, Shan.” Bo was in the driver’s seat, Sniper outside his window with his arm resting on the roof of the truck. “I’m gonna be lucky if I get ten bucks from the scrapyard. Looks like hitchin’s gonna have to be the way after all. It’ll be fine.”“谢了，珊。”博坐在驾驶座上，斯奈珀站在他车窗外，胳膊搭在卡车车顶上。“我要是能从废品站换到十块钱，就算走运了。看来到头来还是得搭便车。会没事的。”

“Hm.”“嗯。”

Truckers and meat hooks.卡车司机和肉钩。

The attendant had a death wish.那名随从简直是活得不耐烦了。

Sniper could see everything the attendant was. Handsome, kind, sweet, loving, trusting, hopeful, eager, passive, weak, cowardly, naive, helpless, stupid. Soft. Nobody. Corpse.Sniper 能把那名侍者的一切都看得清清楚楚。英俊、善良、温柔、有爱心、信任他人、满怀希望、热切、被动、软弱、怯懦、天真、无助、愚蠢。心软。无名之辈。尸体。

“Right then,” Sniper said. “Want a tip for the road?”“那好吧，”狙击手说，“临别前要给你个忠告吗？”

“Yeah, sure.”“好啊，当然。”

“When some bastard gets fresh with you…” He looked at the attendant significantly. “When some bastard gets fresh with you, you know what you should do?”“要是哪个混蛋对你动手动脚……”他意味深长地看了那名服务员一眼，“要是哪个混蛋对你动手动脚，你知道该怎么做吧？”

He smiled in a here we go again kind of way. “What?”他露出一种“又来了”式的笑容。“什么？”

“Swift kick to the nadgers.”“对准蛋蛋来一记飞踢。”

The attendant laughed.侍从笑了。

“Thumbs to the eyes.”“大拇指戳眼。”

The laugh became uneasy. The attendant didn’t like dark jokes. It wasn’t a joke.笑声变得不安起来。那名侍从不喜欢黑色笑话。可这并不是玩笑。

“Press.” Sniper leaned close to the attendant, whose eyes were wide and exposed. “Til you hear the crunch.”“按。”狙击手凑近那名侍者，后者双眼圆睁，毫无遮掩。“一直按到听见咔嚓一声为止。”

The attendant stopped laughing. He waited for Sniper to smile or chuckle or do anything to lighten the mood.侍从不再笑了。他等着 Sniper 微笑、轻笑，或做点什么来缓和气氛。

“Bone’s thinner at the back of the eye sockets. Known as flaccid paralysis, if you punch yer thumbs through correctly. That’s when they just flop over because you poked a hole in the brain’s frontal lobe. Might not kill, but nobody’s gettin’ back up from that. If you can’t get in hard enough to break the bone, you can just twist–““眼窝后侧的骨头更薄。要是拇指捅对了位置，这就叫弛缓性瘫痪。那时他们会直接瘫软下去，因为你在大脑额叶上戳了个洞。可能不会致命，但没人能再爬起来。要是你没法用力捅进去把骨头弄断，那就直接一拧——”

“Stop!”“停下！”

“–your thumbs ‘round in there and just scoop the eyes right out. Piece of piss. Very disorientin’ to have them dangling like that, trust me. Then you–”“——把两根拇指伸进去转一圈，直接把眼珠子抠出来。小菜一碟。相信我，让它们就那么耷拉着，会让人晕头转向得厉害。然后你就——”

“Shan!”“Shan！”

“–grab his keys and wallet, kick him out, and ride off. Free car and cash that way. You could kill him, if you have the stones for it. No witnesses that way, but then you’d have a body. But you’re a proper American bloke, aren’t ya? Must’ve butchered a deer at least once in your life, yeah?”“——抢走他的钥匙和钱包，把他踹下车，然后开车走人。这样就能白得一辆车和一笔现金。你可以杀了他，只要你有这个胆量。那样就没有目击者了，可你也就多了一具尸体要处理。不过你可是个地道的美国佬，对吧？你这辈子总该至少宰过一次鹿吧，嗯？”

The attendant looked afraid. He could stand to be terrified. Sniper loomed. He was good at looming, especially over somebody who was just a lamb.那名服务员看上去很害怕。他真该被吓个半死。狙击手的身影压了过来。他很擅长给人这种压迫感，尤其当对方不过是一只羔羊时。

“Wild animals is always keen for easy meat.”“野兽总是喜欢容易到口的肉。”

Sniper reached into his vest. The attendant flinched back and shut his easily scoopable eyes. When he opened them, Sniper was holding a roll of bills to him. Just a fraction of the cash he had on him at all times, in case things went pear-shaped and he had to go on the run. The attendant took the money with a shaky hand, thumbed through it. It wasn’t much.狙击手把手伸进背心。服务员吓得往后一缩，闭上了那双看上去很容易被挖出来的眼睛。等他睁开眼时，狙击手正把一卷钞票递到他面前。那不过是他一直随身携带的现金中的一小部分，以防事情出了岔子，他不得不跑路。服务员用颤抖的手接过钱，用拇指捻了捻。没多少钱。

It wasn’t much to Sniper. The attendant’s shakes went from his hand to the rest of his body, all the way to his eyes. The attendant dropped the cash like it would bite him, and it rolled under the seat. Now he was terrified. It had been a while since Sniper had seen somebody become so small. The attendant wouldn’t look at him –couldn’t look at him– and he had a thready, squeaky laugh that was on its way to becoming a sob. His eyes were very shiny at the edges, and his normally golden skin was very green. He was the sort of green that might keep him alive.乘务员把现金丢下，像是怕那钱会咬他似的，钱滚到了座位底下。这下他吓坏了。狙击手已经很久没见过有人能缩得这么小。乘务员不肯看他——没法看他——只发出一阵细弱尖细的笑声，那笑声正渐渐变成抽泣。他的眼角亮得厉害，平时金黄色的皮肤此刻绿得吓人。他绿成了那种兴许反倒能让他活命的绿色。

“Get a new truck,” Sniper said. He touched the brim of his hat of his hat and took a step back. “Safe travels.”“买辆新卡车吧，”狙击手说。他碰了碰帽檐，后退一步。“一路平安。”

When Sniper been a boy, he’d caught a bird had gotten into the house. What exact species it had been he couldn’t remember, but it had been was one of those little common birds you could find anywhere. Pointless to kill it, since it had been so small and not even a pest. He remembered the feeling of the little soft body going very still, while the heart was going so fast it was vibrating. It had been so light it had been like holding nothing at all. After looking at it for a while, he’d taken it outside, careful not to accidentally crush it, and opened his hands. The bird just stayed there in his palms, paralyzed with fear and the prey instinct to play dead. When it realized it could escape, it shot off into the bush. If it ever came back to the station, he wouldn’t have known; it would have just blended in with all the other identical common birds. It had been unremarkable.Sniper 小时候，曾抓到过一只闯进屋里的鸟。他已经记不清那到底是什么品种，只记得是那种随处可见的普通小鸟。杀它没什么意义，因为它那么小，甚至算不上害鸟。他记得那柔软的小身体渐渐僵住不动，而心跳却快得发颤。它轻得仿佛手里什么都没托着。看了一会儿后，他把它带到屋外，小心翼翼地生怕一个不慎把它捏坏，然后张开了双手。那只鸟就那样待在他掌心里，被恐惧和装死的猎物本能定住了。等它意识到自己可以逃走，便嗖地窜进了灌木丛。它后来有没有再飞回驻地，他也不会知道；它只会和其他所有一模一样的普通小鸟混在一起。它毫不起眼。

Funny, the memories that came back to you sometimes.说来有趣，有时候回忆会自己浮现在你脑海里。

----

Compared to the outside, the motel room stank of sex. The Spy was still in the bed, still lounging, still smoking, still affecting indifference, and still hard.与外面相比，汽车旅馆的房间里弥漫着性爱的气味。那个间谍仍躺在床上，仍懒散地歪靠着，仍抽着烟，仍装出一副漫不经心的样子，而且下身还硬着。

“That thing ever gonna go down?”“那玩意儿到底会不会落下来？”

“Are you offering to help?” the Spy answered. He crossed a leg over the other. “I heard our beau leaving at some speed. I assume that means you made a hash of your goodbye.”“你这是在主动帮忙吗？”间谍答道。他翘起一条腿搭在另一条腿上。“我听见咱们的情郎急匆匆地走了。我猜那说明你的告别搞砸了。”

“Weren’t listening at the door this time, sneak?”“这次没在门口偷听吧，小滑头？”

“It’s difficult to get up at the moment. Well?”“现在起床有点困难。怎么样？”

Sniper shrugged.狙击手耸了耸肩。

“Fah. Just terrible.”“呸。简直太糟了。”

“Get out.”“出去。”

“Another awful goodbye. Try again.”“又是一次糟糕的告别。再试一次。”

“You can get out yourself, or I can throw you out starkers. Your choice.”“你可以自己出去，或者我可以把你光着身子扔出去。你自己选。”

“Ugh.” The Spy squirmed on the bed. “Show some pity. You almost succeeded in bisecting me.”“呃。”间谍在床上扭动着身体。“发发慈悲吧。你差一点就把我一分为二了。”

“Not my fault. That’s you and the sex maniac pills you dosed us with.”“不怪我。要怪就怪你，还有你给我们灌的那些发情药。”

“Yes, blame chemistry,” the Spy said with a quirked eyebrow. “Blame me. Blame everything and everyone but yourself. As if I made you do, or take, or give me anything, bushman. You could stop whenever you want, and yet… Haaa, but you must think yourself terribly weak.”“是啊，怪化学反应吧，”间谍挑了挑眉说。“怪我吧。怪一切、怪所有人，就是不怪你自己。说得好像我逼你做事、逼你吃药，或者逼你给我什么东西似的，丛林佬。你随时都可以停下，可偏偏……哈啊，不过你肯定觉得自己弱得不得了。”

“Hrm.”“嗯。”

“If you were so easy to subdue, it would be you lying here in agony instead of the other way around.” He smiled knowingly. “How good of our dear beau to succeed where I failed. And to have done decent job, by the sounds I heard. I must ask him how he managed to persuade you.”“如果你真那么容易制服，现在躺在这儿痛苦不堪的就该是你，而不是像现在这样反过来。”他意味深长地笑了笑。“我们亲爱的情郎可真行，在我失败的地方成功了。而且听我听到的动静，还干得挺不错。我得问问他到底是怎么说服你的。”

“He weren’t you,” Sniper said, hoping it would sting.“他可不像你，”狙击手说，希望这话能刺痛对方。

“Is that all? Get me my disguise kit. I’ve already stolen his face.” He cleared his throat. “C’mon, Shan. Want me to do ya again? God, your voice is so h-h-hot.”“就这些？把我的易容工具包拿来。我已经把他的脸偷到手了。”他清了清嗓子。“来吧，珊。想让我再干你一次？天啊，你的声音可真性 - 性 - 性感。”

“Creep,” Sniper said. “Hope you have fun seein’ him in the mirror, then. Headed for the hills, that one. Won’t be seein’ him for a long time.”“变态，”狙击手说。“那你就好好享受在镜子里见到他吧。那家伙往山里跑了。会有好长一段时间见不着他了。”

The Spy frowned at him. “You disgusting jarman. What the hell did you say to him?”间谍冲他皱起眉头。“你这恶心的 jarman。你到底跟他说了什么？”

“He’ll live. Get out.”“他死不了。滚出去。”

“Fine. Fetch me a towel first, chien.”“行吧。先给我拿条毛巾来，chien。”

“Mm.”“嗯。”

He fetched the thin damp towel and watched the spook clean himself off. The Spy paid special attention to between his legs. It needed it.他拿来那条薄薄的湿毛巾，看着那个密探把自己擦干净。这名间谍格外仔细地清理了两腿之间。那地方确实需要擦一擦。

“And he calls me a creep,” the Spy said, glancing at Sniper. “Stop staring, you deviant.”“他还说我是变态，”间谍说着瞥了狙击手一眼。“别盯着看了，你这个死变态。”

“Hm.” He didn’t meet the other man’s gaze. There were more interesting things to look at. “Tender?”“嗯。”他没有迎上另一个男人的目光。有更有趣的东西可看。“温柔？”

“What an idiotic question,” the Spy huffed. “How could I not be? You two made such at effort at filling my ass with foutre it was like you wanted to make it spill from my mouth.”“这问题真蠢，”间谍哼了一声，“我怎么可能不呢？你们俩费了那么大劲把我的屁股灌满精液，简直像是想让它从我嘴里溢出来。”

Sniper blinked. The Spy continued cleaning himself.狙击手眨了眨眼。间谍继续清理着自己。

“Get on your belly.”“趴下。”

“Hm?” The Spy paused his wiping, covering himself with ineffective modesty.“嗯？”间谍停下了擦拭的动作，用徒劳的矜持遮住自己。

From the side of the bed, as he loomed over the naked man, “Get. On. Your. Belly.”他从床边居高临下地逼近那个赤裸的男人：“趴。下。”

“Please,” he answered, deadpan. Sniper could see the obvious twitch behind the towel. “Have mercy.”“求你了，”他面无表情地回答。狙击手能看见毛巾后面那明显的抽动。“发发慈悲吧。”

Sniper breathed out through his nose.狙击手从鼻子里呼出一口气。

The Spy obeyed slowly. By the way he moved, it was difficult to tell if he was actually in pain or just pretending. Couldn’t be that much pain if he could still smoke and look back at Sniper with such a snooty expression. Sniper put a knee on the bed and looked down at the prone man. He wasn’t sure what he was going to do next, but whatever he did, he’d blame it on the chemistry. He took a palmful of meager bumcheek in each hand. God, the Spy could use it amazingly, but…间谍慢慢地照做了。看他移动的样子，很难判断他是真的疼还是只是装的。如果还能抽着烟、用那么傲慢的表情回头看狙击手，那就不可能有多疼。狙击手把一边膝盖压到床上，俯视着趴着的男人。他不确定接下来要做什么，但不管做什么，他都会把责任推给化学反应。他每只手都抓了满满一把瘦削的屁股肉。天哪，这间谍可真会用它，但……

“Charmant,” the Spy returned. He lifted his arse against Sniper palms with an annoyed sigh. “Thankless, spoiled beast. You don’t know how to appreciate a good thing when you literally have it in your hands. Just wait until it’s gone.”“ Charmant，”间谍回道。他烦躁地叹了口气，把屁股抬起来贴到狙击手的手掌上。“不知感恩的娇惯畜生。好东西明明就握在你手里，你却不懂得珍惜。等失去了你就知道了。”

Then Sniper was struck with horror. He pressed his face to the Spy’s lower back and groaned with misery.随后，狙击手惊恐万分。他把脸贴在间谍的后腰上，痛苦地呻吟起来。

“Oh, for God’s sake, what are you howling about now?”“哦，看在上帝的份上，你现在又在嚎什么？”

Sniper continued to groan.狙击手继续呻吟着。

“What?”“什么？”

“I didn’t bugger him tonight,” Sniper said mournfully as he squeezed the Spy’s arse. “And he left.”“我今晚没操他，”狙击手一边揉着间谍的屁股，一边哀怨地说。“而且他走了。”

“What?” When Sniper squeezed again, full of despondency, the Spy understood. The cigarette fell from his mouth in shock as he realized. “No…”“什么？”当狙击手又一次捏紧，满脸沮丧时，间谍明白了。他震惊地意识到这一点，嘴里的香烟都掉了下来。“不……”

“Yeah.”“是啊。”

“You idiot! I can’t believe you just got rid of the most glorious ass in Teufort! Quite possibly all of New Mexico! Ingrate!” He put his face in his hands. “How could you do this to me?!”“你这个白痴！我真不敢相信你居然把特夫特最完美的屁股给弄没了！说不定是整个新墨西哥州最完美的！白眼狼！”他把脸埋进双手里。“你怎么能这样对我？！”

“That bottom… That bottom was worth bottling.”“那个屁股……那个屁股真值得装瓶珍藏。”

“Une boule merveilleuse.”“一个奇妙的圆球。”

“Amazing cushion.”“超棒的坐垫。”

“A pearl. Two pearls.”“一颗珍珠。两颗珍珠。”

“Beauty.”“美。”

“His ass could have been sculpted by Italian masters.”“他的屁股简直像是意大利大师雕刻出来的。”

“Belonged in a museum.”“该进博物馆。”

“If it had been in a museum, I would have stolen it.” The BLU Spy kicked him, legs suddenly very functional as he continued to furiously harangue Sniper. “And you scared him away! Don’t you every think before you say anything? Why can’t you ever keep your mouth shut? Get off me!”“要是它摆在博物馆里，我早就把它偷走了。” BLU 间谍踢了他一脚，双腿突然又利索起来，一边继续对狙击手怒斥不休。“而你吓跑了他！你开口之前难道就不能动动脑子吗？你怎么就不能管住你那张嘴？从我身上滚开！”

“It ain’t my fault! It was all your flash Spy stories, you rat bastard!” he snapped back.“这不能怪我！全怪你那些花里胡哨的间谍故事，你这鼠辈混蛋！”他厉声回敬道。

“Damn you, bushman! How is a disgusting camper van at all inspirational? He would have stayed here dreaming of better things if it weren’t for you!” He screamed further insults into a pillow.“该死的，你这个野人！一辆恶心的露营车到底哪里鼓舞人心了？要不是你，他本来会留在这里，憧憬更美好的事物！”他对着枕头又尖声咒骂了一通。

Sniper considered pressing his face into it harder until all the sound stopped. Instead, he hung his head, miserable as a bandicoot. “Gone. Bastard. Swannin’ in here with your fancy talk an’ mind games an’ dope an’ makin’ it all about you. Selfish bloody prima donna. Gone.”狙击手考虑过把脸更用力地埋进去，直到所有声音都消失。但他只是垂下头，像只袋狸似的可怜巴巴。“走了。混蛋。大摇大摆地晃进来，满嘴花里胡哨的说辞，玩心理把戏，还嗑药，把一切都弄得围着你转。自私的该死的臭屁大牌。走了。”

“I can track him down,” the Spy declared, raising his head. “Convince him to stay. Yes, that’s simple enough. Once I can walk. And it’s not like he can get very far with any speed. Not with that collapsing truck of his. Everything will be fine. Yes. Yes, everything will be fine, just fine. I can fix this.”“我能追踪到他，”间谍抬起头，断然说道。“说服他留下。对，这够简单。等我能够走路以后。而且他就算开得再快也跑不了多远，尤其还开着他那辆快散架的卡车。一切都会没事的。是的。是的，一切都会没事的，肯定没事。我能搞定这件事。”

“I hate you,” said the Spy.“我恨你，”间谍说。

“Hell,” answered Sniper. “Me too.”“见鬼，”狙击手答道，“我也是。”
